Title: State lawmakers consider data center testimony - FarmWeekNow
Summary_AI: Illinois lawmakers are advancing 21 data center-related bills through House and Senate committees, with testimony from utility, environmental, labor, and agricultural groups highlighting concerns about grid capacity, electricity costs, water usage, and farmland impacts. The Illinois Farm Bureau expressed support for reasonable data center development conditional on developers paying their share of energy costs, implementing water management practices, and providing financial assurances for site decommissioning. Ameren Illinois testified that utilities are implementing "cost causation" principles to ensure data center developers pay for the additional electrical demand their facilities create and that all large load projects require detailed engineering reviews to confirm grid reliability.

Title: Interview: Unison Energy CEO on Data Centers Turning to On-Site Power
Summary_AI: Unison Energy, a Connecticut-based Energy-as-a-Service company, is capitalizing on interconnection delays by deploying on-site natural gas-based microgrids and combined heat and power systems for data center projects across North America. CEO Mariko McDonagh Meier noted that developers are increasingly shifting from grid-dependent designs to pairing compute infrastructure with dispatchable on-site generation as a primary power source rather than backup, accelerated by interconnection queues exceeding 2 TW of capacity awaiting approval. The company's pipeline includes recent deployments like a CHP system for General Mills in Missouri, with data center power demand projected to reach 325-580 TWh by 2028, up from 176 TWh in 2023. This trend reflects a fundamental reshaping of AI infrastructure construction, where securing dedicated on-site power enables faster project development timelines than waiting for grid upgrades.

Title: Qualcomm Stock Is the Sleeping Giant of the AI Revolution. It's Starting to Wake Up.
Summary_AI: Qualcomm is pivoting its "cold chip" engineering expertise, previously focused on power efficiency for mobile, to address the growing demand for AI inference in data centers. Qualcomm, Inc_ logo on phone-by viewimage via Shutterstock

More than that, the company has carried a heavy overhang of risks, from intense pressure from Chinese vendors to the gradual transition of Apple (AAPL) to its own in-house chips.

Summary_AI: Kio Data Centers has signed a 10-year Power Purchase Agreement with Celsia to supply power for its data center operations in Panama. Article_Text:
Kio Data Centers signs 10-year PPA with Celsia to power its data center operations in Panama - report
Volume of supply not disclosed
May 26, 2026 By Zachary Skidmore Have your say
Kio Data Centers, a Mexican-based operator, has signed a 10-year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Colombian energy company Celsia to supply power for its Panamanian data center operations.
â€“ Gobierno de PanamÃ¡
First reported by Bnamericas, the PPA is the companyâ€™s first to be recorded in Panama. The volume of supply set to be provided to Kio was not disclosed.

â€œThis partnership positions Kio Data Centers as one of the providers with the highest level of energy certainty in the region,â€ the company added.

Title: Midwest Demand Growth Drives $1.5B Columbia Gas Expansion - East Daley Analytics
Summary_AI: TC Energy is investing $1.5 billion in an expansion of its Columbia Gas system, named Appalachian Supply, to meet projected load growth of 4 Bcf/d by 2035. Driven by increasing natural gas demand from data centers and power plants in the Midwest, the 800 MMcf/d expansion is backed by a 20-year contract and is expected to be in-service by 2030. This project is part of TC Energy's strategy to connect low-cost supply to systems serving long-duration demand, positioning itself to capitalize on growth across the Midwest and Northeast.
Article_Text:
MIDWEST DEMAND GROWTH DRIVES $1.5B COLUMBIA GAS EXPANSION
Midwest, Natural Gas, Northeast, TC Energy, The Daley Note
East Daley Analytics
TC Energy (TRP) plans to invest $1.5B to meet load growth on the Columbia Gas system, part of a trend of growing natural gas demand from data centers and power plants based in the Midwest.
TRP announced the expansion, the Appalachian Supply project, on May 1 in its 1Q26 earnings update. The 800 MMcf/d expansion is backed by a 20-year contract with an investor-grade utility and has an expected build multiple of 7.3x, the company said. The project will serve new power generation load.
Appalachian Supply has an anticipated in-service date in 2030, and can potentially be expanded up to 2 Bcf/d with additional compression. On the earnings call, executives said they expect demand on the Columbia Gas system will expand 4 Bcf/d by 2035.
Columbia Gas Transmission extends from Ohio through the mid-Atlantic region. The sprawling system spans nearly 12,000 miles and 10 states, connecting to Appalachian production and storage, as well as major interstate pipelines like ANR, Texas Eastern, Tennessee, and Panhandle Eastern.
East Daley has highlighted the outlook for growing gas demand in the Midwest, spurred by data center development and opportunities to convert older coal plants. TC Energy owns several key pipelines in the region, including ANR, Columbia Gas and Crossroads, and is well positioned to capitalize on this growth (see map from TRP investor relations).
The company recently completed two successful non-binding open seasons that confirm the market upside.
One, an open season to expand Columbia Gas to serve new load in the Columbus, OH area, closed on Jan. 9. That project had targeted 500 MMcf of new capacity, yet the open season received ~1.5 Bcf/d in total bids, TRP said. It is unclear if Appalachian Supply is designed to meet customer interest from that open season.

Title: Generac surges as Jefferies upgrades to buy on AI infrastructure boom - MSN
Summary_AI: Jefferies upgraded Generac to Buy, citing its potential to secure major hyperscaler data center contracts related to the AI infrastructure boom. Generac is reportedly nearing a final agreement with a hyperscaler, having already received a non-binding $600 million notice to proceed. The company's Baudouin engines are also being integrated into hyperscaler configurations, indicating market acceptance.
Article_Text:
Generac (GNRC) up 7.5% in Friday's trading as Jefferies upgrades shares to Buy from Hold with a $302 price target, raised from $239, saying the manufacturer of backup power generation products is nearing a "moment of truth" in securing major hyperscaler data center contracts tied to the AI infrastructure boom.
Dyson Memorial Day Sales Event
"Given the continued strong environment for data center development, and potential indications of activity with hyperscalers, we see an asymmetric positive risk/reward setup" for Generac (GNRC), according to Jefferies analysts led by Tanner James.
Generac (GNRC) proclaimed in April to be on the "one-yard line" in negotiations toward a final agreement with its first hyperscaler with a non-binding $600M notice to proceed already disclosed; "process timing can be notoriously fickle, but we feel incrementally confident in [management's] ability to convert, James says.
While long-term execution in the data center market remains uncertain given entrenched competition, there are multiple potential contracts in the works, the analyst says, adding that Baudouin engines are finding their way into hyperscaler configurations, pointing to market acceptance for a product only Generac (GNRC) can ably scale.
Finally, Generac (GNRC) shares are "pricing in less while potentially offering more" after correcting 12% from their post-Q1 reporting high, James says.
